evidence.note: Discovered a falsified assumption (missing workspace deps + no-Cargo.toml-edits rule) and re-derived the storage design around available dependencies instead of forcing it.
Chosen implementation approach (delegating schema generation to a subagent) failed/stalled; agent cleanly abandoned it and built types directly.

Strongest adaptation: recognized Storage trait return-type was wrong from test evidence, called it a structural issue, revised the trait AND propagated the corrected contract (and later error type) across memory.rs/etcd.rs — anchor-8 style propagation.

Repeated duplicate-type collisions resolved at the design level by choosing a single definition and re-exporting (ObjectReference, UserInfo, CSIVolumeSource, HostPathVolumeSource) rather than patching each call site.
Large stretch of reactive single-call-site type fixes (Option<T> vs T, field renames) with repeated rewrites of the same common files — symptom-level patching and notable churn, closer to anchor 3-5.
Persistent EndpointSlice ports mismatch: re-investigated across files repeatedly rather than blindly repeating, showing course-correction impulse though somewhat circular.

reasoning: The agent consistently treats compile/test failures as signal and backs out wrong per-crate assumptions (anchor 5), and in the Storage-trait/error-type case and the duplicate-type consolidations it propagated a corrected contract fact across all affected files and shared abstractions (anchor 8 behavior). However, it never established the contract up front, and a large fraction of the trajectory is reactive one-mismatch-at-a-time patching with heavy rewriting of the same files — falling short of the proactive, churn-avoiding re-derivation described at level 10. This places observed behavior between anchors 5 and 8, at a 6.
